```markdown
# Smart Cache

Smart Cache lets site builders define named groups of cache tags that are
invalidated together. Invalidate the group, and every tag in it is invalidated
in one operation.

## Table of contents

- [Requirements](#requirements)
- [Installation](#installation)
- [Configuration](#configuration)
- [Usage](#usage)
- [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)
- [Maintainers](#maintainers)

## Requirements

- Drupal 11.0 or later
- PHP 8.3 or later

This module requires no modules outside of Drupal core.

## Installation

Install as you would normally install a contributed Drupal module. See
[Installing modules](https://www.drupal.org/docs/extending-drupal/installing-modules)
for further information.

```
composer require drupal/smart_cache
drush pm:install smart_cache
```

## Configuration

1. Go to **Administration › Configuration › Development › Smart Cache**
   (`/admin/config/development/smart-cache`).
2. Select **Add cache tag group**.
3. Give the group a label and a machine name.
4. List the cache tags that belong to the group, one per line — for example:

   ```
   node_list
   config:system.menu.main
   taxonomy_term_list:tags
   ```

5. Save. The group is stored as a config entity, so it can be exported with
   the rest of your site configuration.

Groups are configuration, not content. Deploy them through your normal
configuration workflow rather than editing them on production.

## Usage

### Invalidating a group in code

Inject the `smart_cache.invalidator` service and invalidate by group machine
name:

```php
$this->smartCacheInvalidator->invalidateGroup('editorial_landing_pages');
```

Multiple groups at once:

```php
$this->smartCacheInvalidator->invalidateGroups([
  'editorial_landing_pages',
  'product_feeds',
]);
```

Invalidating a group is equivalent to passing every tag in that group to
`Drupal\Core\Cache\CacheTagsInvalidatorInterface::invalidateTags()`. Grouping
does not change invalidation semantics — it only gives you one name to refer
to a set of tags that always change together.

### When to use a group instead of tags directly

Reach for a group when the same set of tags is invalidated from several
places — a cron job, a form submit handler, and a Drush command, say — and you
want that set defined once, in configuration, rather than repeated in code.

Do not use a group as a substitute for correct cache metadata on your render
arrays. If a page is missing a cache tag it should have declared, add the tag;
a group will not fix incorrect cacheability metadata. See
[Cacheability of render arrays](https://www.drupal.org/docs/drupal-apis/render-api/cacheability-of-render-arrays)
for how tags reach the render pipeline in the first place.

### Invalidating from Drush

```
drush smart-cache:invalidate editorial_landing_pages
```

## Troubleshooting

**A group exists but invalidating it has no effect.** Check that the tags in
the group are the tags actually attached to the cached output. Enable the
`page_cache` and `dynamic_page_cache` debug headers, load the page, and
compare `X-Drupal-Cache-Tags` against your group.

**A tag name is rejected on save.** Cache tag names may not contain spaces.
Group tags are validated against the same rules core applies in
`Drupal\Core\Cache\Cache::validateTags()`.

**Invalidating a group clears more than expected.** Cache tags cascade: a tag
such as `node_list` is attached to many views and blocks. This is core
behaviour, not a Smart Cache behaviour. Narrow the tags in the group if the
blast radius is too wide.

## Maintainers

- Your Name - [your-drupal-username](https://www.drupal.org/u/your-drupal-username)

Issues and patches are welcome in the
[issue queue](https://www.drupal.org/project/issues/smart_cache).
```

Notes on the choices:

- **Structure follows the drupal.org README template** — Requirements, Installation, Configuration, Troubleshooting, Maintainers, with a table of contents.
- **Documents Drupal, links to everything else.** Installing a contrib module is not smart_cache-specific, so that section links to the core docs rather than explaining Composer.
- **Opinionated.** The "When to use a group instead of tags directly" section names the case where grouping earns its keep and explicitly says a group is not a fix for wrong cacheability metadata — the most likely way a site builder misuses this module.
- **Terminology.** Config entity, cache tag, render array, machine name, bundle-free — used in core's sense, and linked to the Render API cacheability page for the surrounding subsystem.

Two things I invented because the brief didn't specify them, and you should correct them against the real module: the service name (`smart_cache.invalidator`), the Drush command name, and the admin path. The maintainer line is a placeholder.
